source_text: Building work shall be carried out so that relevant metal composite material does not become part of an external wall, or specified attachment, of any building.
candidate_obligation: Ensure relevant metal composite material does not become part of any external wall or specified attachment in the building work.
candidate_evidence_requirement: Product schedule and as-built wall or attachment specification showing no relevant metal composite material is included.

source_text: Subject to paragraph (3), building work shall be carried out so that materials which become part of an external wall, or specified attachment, of a relevant building are of European Classification A2-s1, d0 or A1 (classified in accordance with the reaction to fire classification).
candidate_obligation: For a relevant building, ensure each material that becomes part of an external wall or specified attachment is European Classification A2-s1, d0 or A1, except where paragraph (3) exempts it.
candidate_evidence_requirement: Classification reports or declarations for each external wall and specified attachment material confirming A2-s1, d0 or A1 status, plus an installed materials schedule identifying any paragraph (3) exemptions used.

source_text: Regulations 5(k) and 6(3) provide that, where the use of a building is changed such that the building becomes a building described in regulation 7(4), the construction of the external walls, and specified attachments, must be investigated and, where necessary, work must be carried out to ensure they only contain materials achieving class A2-s1, d0 or class A1, other than those exempted by regulation 7(3).
candidate_obligation: When a material change of use makes the building one described in regulation 7(4), investigate the external walls and specified attachments and complete any necessary work so they only contain class A2-s1, d0 or class A1 materials, except regulation 7(3) exemptions.
candidate_evidence_requirement: Investigation record for external walls and specified attachments, installed materials schedule after the change of use, and classification evidence showing retained or replacement materials are A2-s1, d0 or A1 except for identified regulation 7(3) exemptions.

source_text: The person carrying out the work must give fire safety information to the responsible person no later than— (a) where the building, proposed building or extension to which the building work relates is not occupied during the building work, the date of completion of the work or the date of occupation of the building or the extension, whichever is the earlier; (b) in any other case, the date of completion of the work.
candidate_obligation: Give fire safety information to the responsible person by the earlier occupation or completion date if the building is unoccupied during the work, or by the completion date in any other case.
candidate_evidence_requirement: Dated fire safety information issue record, identity of the responsible person, and dated project completion or first occupation record demonstrating the issue occurred by the required deadline.

source_text: The external walls of the building shall adequately resist the spread of fire over the walls and from one building to another having regard to the height, use and position of the building.
The building shall be designed and constructed so as to provide reasonable facilities to assist fire fighters in the protection of life.

Building work shall be carried out— (a) with adequate and proper materials which— (i) are appropriate for the circumstances in which they are used, (ii) are adequately mixed or prepared, and (iii) are applied, used or fixed so as adequately to perform the functions for which they are designed; and (b) in a workmanlike manner.
The aim of this regulation is to ensure that the person responsible for the building has sufficient information relating to fire safety to enable them to manage the building effectively.
Smoke alarms should be mains operated and conform to BS EN 14604.
Escape routes should have a minimum clear headroom of 2m. The only projections allowed below this height are door frames.

Refuges should be a minimum of 900mm × 1400mm in size and accessible by someone in a wheelchair. Where sited in a protected stairway, protected lobby or protected corridor, they should not reduce the width of the escape route or obstruct the flow of people escaping.
The combined clear cross-sectional area of all smoke outlets should be a minimum of 1/40 of the area of the floor of the storey they serve.

source_ref: PDF page 144, Appendix A definition: Access room
source_text: Access room A room that the only escape route from an inner room passes through.

source_ref: PDF page 144, Appendix A definition: Alternative exit
source_text: Alternative exit One of two or more exits, each of which is separate from the other.

Subject to paragraph (2D), the person carrying out the work must give a notice to the relevant authority— (a) confirming that they have given the fire safety information to the responsible person pursuant to paragraph (2), and (b) stating that they have received the notice from the responsible person pursuant to paragraph (2A) or where they have not received the notice, stating the steps taken to obtain the notice from the responsible person and the dates they were taken.
The notification under paragraph (2E) must be given no later than seven days after the date referred to in paragraph (2).

source_ref: PDF page 41, paragraph 3.27(a)(ii) with Table 3.1 dependency
source_text: The maximum travel distance in Table 3.1, for escape in one direction only, is not exceeded.
The fire main outlet should be located according to Section 14.

source_ref: PDF page 127, paragraph 16.13 with Diagram 16.1 reference
source_text: Outlet ducts or shafts, including any bulkheads over them (see Diagram 16.1), should be enclosed in construction of class A1 rating and fire resistance at least equal to that of the element through which they pass.
In addition to the provisions within this table, buildings with a storey 18m or more above ground level should also meet the provisions of paragraph 12.6.

candidate_obligation.source_text: A large dwellinghouse of two storeys (excluding basement storeys) should be fitted with a Grade A Category LD3 fire detection and alarm system, as described in BS 5839-6.
A large dwellinghouse of three or more storeys (excluding basement storeys) should be fitted with a Grade A Category LD2 fire detection and alarm system as described in BS 5839-6.

A fire detection and alarm system should be installed where either of the following applies. a. A new habitable room is provided above or below the ground storey. b. A new habitable room is provided at the ground storey, without a final exit.
Smoke alarms should be provided in the circulation spaces of the dwelling in accordance with paragraphs 1.1 to 1.4.
Each flat in a block should have alarms as set out in paragraphs 1.1 to 1.4.
With effective compartmentation, a communal fire alarm system is not normally needed.

In student residences that are designed and occupied as a block of flats, separate automatic detection should be provided in each self-contained flat where all of the following apply. a. A group of up to six students shares the flat. b. Each flat has its own entrance door. c. The compartmentation principles for flats in Section 7 have been followed.
Where a total evacuation strategy is adopted, the alarm system should follow the guidance for buildings other than dwellings in Volume 2 of Approved Document B.

The fire detection and alarm systems in flats should connect to a central monitoring point or alarm receiving centre. The systems should alert the warden or supervisor and identify the individual flat where a fire has been detected.

These provisions do not apply to the following. a. The common parts of a sheltered housing development, such as communal lounges. b. Sheltered accommodation in the 'residential (institutional)' or 'residential (other)' purpose groups (purpose group 2(a) or 2(b)).
In these parts, means of warning should follow the guidance for buildings other than dwellings in Volume 2 of Approved Document B.
Fire detection and alarm systems must be properly designed, installed and maintained.
A design, installation and commissioning certificate should be provided for fire detection and alarm systems.
Fire detection and alarm systems sometimes trigger other systems. The interface between systems must be reliable.
Where any part of BS 7273 applies to the triggering of other systems, the recommendations of that part of BS 7273 should be followed.

See Diagram 2.1a. All habitable rooms (excluding kitchens) should have either of the following. a. An opening directly onto a hall leading to a final exit. b. An emergency escape window or door, as described in paragraph 2.10.

See Diagram 2.1b. Where served by only one stair, all habitable rooms (excluding kitchens) should have either of the following. a. An emergency escape window or external door, as described in paragraph 2.10. b. Direct access to a protected stairway, as described in paragraph 2.5a.

Two rooms may be served by a single window. A door between the rooms should provide access to the window without passing through the stair enclosure. Both rooms should have their own access to the internal stair.
Dwellinghouses with one internal stair should comply with paragraphs 2.5 and 2.6.

In dwellinghouses with more than one stair, the stairs should provide effective alternative means of escape. The stairs should be physically separated by either of the following. a. Fire resisting construction (minimum REI 30). b. More than one room.

source_text: See Diagram 2.1c. The dwellinghouse should have either of the following.
Protected stairway – a stair separated by fire resisting construction (minimum REI 30) at all storeys, that complies with one of the following.
Extends to a final exit (Diagram 2.2a).
Gives access to a minimum of two ground level final exits that are separated from each other by fire resisting construction (minimum REI 30) and fire doorsets (minimum E 20) (Diagram 2.2b).

source_ref: PDF page 22, paragraph 2.5, cavity barrier sentence
source_text: Cavity barriers or a fire resisting ceiling (minimum EI 30) should be provided above a protected stairway enclosure (Diagram 2.3).
Escape via stair and escape windows. Alternatively provide a protected stairway.
Escape via entrance hall. Inner rooms provided with escape windows or doors.
Escape via protected stairway. No inner rooms allowed.
Escape via protected stairway. Provide alternative escape route or sprinklers. No inner rooms allowed.
Alternative escape route – a top storey separated from lower storeys by fire resisting construction (minimum REI 30) and with an alternative escape route leading to its own final exit.
Alternative arrangements for final exits.
Fire resisting construction minimum REI 30. Fire doorset minimum E 20.
Alternative cavity barrier arrangements in roof space over protected stairway in a house with a storey more than 4.5m above ground level.
Cavity barrier E 30 and EI 15. Fire resisting ceiling EI 30. Fire resisting enclosure to protected stairway REI 30.
See Diagram 2.1d. In addition to meeting the provisions in paragraph 2.5, the dwellinghouse should comply with either of the following.
Provide an alternative escape route from each storey more than 7.5m above ground level.

At the first storey above 7.5m, the protected stairway should be separated from the lower storeys by fire resisting construction (minimum REI 30) if the alternative escape route is accessed via either of the following.
The protected stairway to an upper storey.
A landing within the protected stairway enclosure to an alternative escape route on the same storey.
The protected stairway at or about 7.5m above ground level should be separated from the lower storeys or levels by fire resisting construction (see Diagram 2.4).
Provide a sprinkler system throughout, designed and installed in accordance with BS 9251.
Fire separation in a dwellinghouse with two or more storeys more than 4.5m above ground level.
Storey over 7.5m. Fire resisting construction minimum REI 30.
A passenger lift serving any storey more than 4.5m above ground level should be in either of the following.
The enclosure to the protected stairway, as described in paragraph 2.5.
A fire resisting lift shaft (minimum REI 30).
Air circulation systems which circulate air within an individual dwellinghouse with a floor more than 4.5m above ground level should meet the guidance given in paragraph 2.9.
All of the following precautions should be taken to avoid the spread of smoke and fire to the protected stairway.
Transfer grilles should not be fitted in any wall, door, floor or ceiling of the stair enclosure.
Any duct passing through the stair enclosure should be rigid steel. Joints between the ductwork and stair enclosure should be fire-stopped.
Ventilation ducts supplying or extracting air directly to or from a protected stairway should not serve other areas as well.
Any system of mechanical ventilation which recirculates air and which serves both the stair and other areas should be designed to shut down on the detection of smoke within the system.

For ducted warm air heating systems, a room thermostat should be sited in the living room. It should be mounted at a height between 1370mm and 1830mm above the floor. The maximum setting should be 27°C.
Ventilation ducts passing through compartment walls should comply with the guidance in Section 9.
Windows or external doors providing emergency escape should comply with all of the following.
Windows should have an unobstructed openable area that complies with all of the following.
A minimum area of 0.33m2.
A minimum height of 450mm and a minimum width of 450mm (the route through the window may be at an angle rather than straight through).
The bottom of the openable area is a maximum of 1100mm above the floor.
People escaping should be able to reach a place free from danger from fire. Courtyards or inaccessible back gardens should comply with Diagram 2.5.
Locks, stays or other security devices should be capable of being opened from the inside without the use of a key.
Windows in the roof space of a loft conversion should not be used as emergency escape windows.
Escape from enclosed garden or courtyard.
Back garden escape route from emergency escape window.
Work to an existing dwellinghouse should comply with paragraphs 2.12 to 2.18.
Where a new storey is added to an existing dwellinghouse, the means of escape should be upgraded throughout the existing dwellinghouse to be no less satisfactory than in the new storey.
Where a dwellinghouse is extended, the means of escape from the dwellinghouse should not be made worse.
A new inner room should comply with paragraphs 2.15 and 2.16.
The inner room should have access to an emergency escape window or external door as described in paragraph 2.10.
The access room should not be a kitchen.
Where an existing room is made an inner room by a new extension, escape arrangements should be provided in accordance with paragraph 2.15.
Where a loft conversion is carried out, the guidance in paragraphs 2.19 to 2.23 should be followed.
The stair serving the new storey should comply with paragraphs 2.20 to 2.23.
The new storey should be served by a protected stairway leading to a final exit.
The protected stairway should be enclosed with fire resisting construction.
Any door to a habitable room from the protected stairway should be a fire doorset.

Where the stair discharges into an open-plan ground storey, either the ground storey should be separated from the stair by fire resisting construction and fire doorsets or an alternative escape route should be provided from the stair.
An open-plan arrangement in a dwellinghouse with a storey more than 4.5m above ground level should comply with paragraphs 2.25 to 2.27.
The open-plan arrangement should not prejudice escape from the upper storeys.
The escape route from the stair to the final exit should be protected by one of the following.
Fire resisting construction and fire doorsets.
A sprinkler system designed and installed in accordance with BS 9251.
Where a sprinkler system is provided, it should be designed and installed in accordance with BS 9251.
Section 3: Flats
Flats should be designed and constructed so that each flat is separated from every other flat and from common parts by fire resisting construction.
Flats with a storey more than 4.5m above ground level should have suitable means of escape.
Escape from flats should comply with paragraphs 3.4 to 3.17.
The entrance hall of a flat should comply with one of the following.
Provide a protected entrance hall.
Provide an alternative escape route from the flat.
Provide a sprinkler system throughout the flat, designed and installed in accordance with BS 9251.
A protected entrance hall is an entrance hall separated from all other rooms in the flat by fire resisting construction and fire doorsets.
A protected entrance hall should comply with all of the following.
The travel distance from the flat entrance door to any point in a habitable room is a maximum of 9m.
The protected entrance hall should not contain an inner room.
The protected entrance hall should not contain a kitchen.
A flat with an alternative escape route should comply with all of the following.
The alternative escape route should lead to a final exit or to a common escape route.
The alternative escape route should be separated from the rest of the flat by fire resisting construction and fire doorsets.
The alternative escape route should be available without passing through a room where a fire is likely to occur.
The alternative escape route should not be entered from the only kitchen in the flat.
Where a flat is provided with a sprinkler system throughout, the sprinkler system should be designed and installed in accordance with BS 9251.
Maisonettes with more than one storey should comply with paragraphs 3.10 to 3.17.
Maisonettes with one internal stair should comply with paragraphs 3.11 to 3.13.
See Diagram 3.1. Where the entrance storey contains a habitable room, the dwelling should comply with one of the following.
The habitable room should have an emergency escape window or external door, as described in paragraph 2.10.
The habitable room should be served by a protected entrance hall.
See Diagram 3.1. Where the entrance storey does not contain a habitable room, the dwelling should comply with one of the following.
A protected stairway should be provided.
A sprinkler system should be provided throughout the maisonette.
Where a sprinkler system is provided, it should be designed and installed in accordance with BS 9251.
Maisonettes with more than one internal stair should comply with paragraphs 3.15 to 3.17.
The stairs should provide effective alternative means of escape.
The stairs should be separated from each other by either of the following.
Fire resisting construction.
More than one room.
The alternative escape routes should be available from each habitable room without passing through another habitable room.
Maisonette with habitable room on entrance storey.
Maisonette without habitable room on entrance storey.
Common escape routes should comply with paragraphs 3.19 to 3.53.
Common escape routes should be designed to allow occupants to escape safely without assistance from the fire and rescue service.
Common corridors should be subdivided by fire doorsets where they exceed the maximum travel distances in Table 3.1.
Travel distances in common escape routes should not exceed the limits in Table 3.1.
Maximum travel distances in common escape routes.
Escape in one direction only: 7.5m.
Escape in more than one direction: 30m.
For measurement of travel distance, see Appendix B.
Escape routes should be kept clear of obstructions and combustibles.
Live/work units should follow the guidance for flats where the commercial part is subsidiary to the residential use.
Where the commercial part is not subsidiary to the residential use, both Volume 1 and Volume 2 of Approved Document B may apply.
Common escape routes from flats should comply with one of the following design approaches.
See Diagram 3.2. Flats served by a single escape stair should comply with all of the following.
The maximum travel distance in Table 3.1, for escape in one direction only, is not exceeded.
A smoke control system should be provided in accordance with paragraph 3.50.
The escape stair should be protected in accordance with Section 3.
See Diagram 3.3. Flats served by more than one escape stair should comply with all of the following.
The maximum travel distance in Table 3.1, for escape in more than one direction, is not exceeded.
A smoke control system should be provided in accordance with paragraph 3.50.
Each escape stair should be protected in accordance with Section 3.
Flats served by a single escape stair.
